newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian tycoon Hasan grabs business spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian tycoon Hasan grabs business spotlight.

text.p: Tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, a close associate of President Suharto, has taken centre stage in Indonesian business this week, helping broker a massive gold mining deal and becoming head of the country's biggest carmaker.
In less than a week, Hasan wrested a sizeable stake in the huge Busang gold property in East Kalimantan, and on Wednesday was elected president-commissioner of car maker Astra International.
Hasan, who looks younger than his 65 years, formed a close relationship with Suharto during the 1950s when the president was regional military commander in central Java.
"I have been friends with President Suharto since 40 years ago when the communists were still in Indonesia," Hasan told reporters after an Astra shareholders' meeting on Wednesday.
Then-Colonel Suharto was serving under General Gatot Subroto, who took Hasan -- an ethnic Chinese who later converted to Islam -- under his wing.
"Bob Hasan is truly trusted by President Suharto," said economist Christianto Wibisono of the private Indonesia Business Data Centre consultancy.
"If Suharto is the commander in chief, Bob is the fleet commander," he added. "He is sort of good uncle to Suharto's children ... filling the vacuum left by the First Lady's death."
Suharto's wife of 40 years, Tien, died in April last year.
Hasan, a sports lover and Suharto's regular golfing partner, is regarded as a key business adviser to the president.
A Canadian businessman described Hasan as an "extremely influential person who knows how to do business".
"He has a good grasp of details and knows how things work," he said.
Hasan grabbed the spotlight this week when partnership details of the Busang property were made public.
Small Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd, got a 45 percent stake in the property and Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States 15 percent.
Bre-X's Indonesian partners PT Askatindo Karya Minerals and PT Amsya Lyna took 30 percent, with the Indonesian government taking the remaining 10 percent.

Mining sources said Hasan had played a key role in concluding the Busang deal after it threatened to get out of control with international companies -- and members of Suharto's family -- jockeying for position.

Askatindo and Amsya are 50-percent owned by the Hasan-led Nusamba group, which is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto and 10 percent each by Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto.
The Busang property is estimated by Bre-X, which discovered the deposit, to contain 70.95 million ounces of gold worth over $24 billion at current prices.
Not long before his high-profile plunge into the Busang project, Hasan's business life had largely centred on the timber business where he heads a cartel of plywood producers.
The Nusamba group has an 8.83 percent holding in Astra International, making it the third-biggest shareholder.

Hasan is also president commissioner of Bank Umum Nasional, private banks Bank Bukopin and Bank Duta and paper maker PT Kiani Kertas. He is also a commissioner of insurance company PT Tugu Pratama Indonesia.
The Nusamba group announced plans late last month to buy a 49 percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama held by conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers for $311.8 million.

Indocopper has 9.36 percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia, which runs one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in Irian Jaya province. Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc has a 81.28 percent stake in Freeport Indonesia.
